(Australia)|}} | website = {{URL|https://www.dfpcl.com/}} }} '''Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals Corporation Limited''' ('''DFPCL''') is an Indian manufacturer of [[Chemical substance|industrial]] and [[Agrochemical|agricultural]] chemicals, crop nutrients, and [[Fertilizer|fertilisers]].{{Cite web |date=22 October 2012 |title=Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals Corporation Ltd (DFPCL) — Analyst Report |url=https://corporate.indbankonline.com/documents/Deepak%20Fertiliser%20%26%20Petrochemicals%20Ltd.pdf |access-date=23 April 2022 |website=[[Indian Bank|Indbank Merchant Banking Services]] |archive-date=28 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211128021057/https://corporate.indbankonline.com/documents/Deepak%20Fertiliser%20%26%20Petrochemicals%20Ltd.pdf |url-status=dead }} == History == The company was established in 1979 by Chimanlal Mehta born in [[Jain]] family from Gujarat, as a private limited company and became public limited in 1982.{{cite web |author=Datta, Aveek |date=7 September 2017 |title=Deepak Fertilisers: On fertile ground |url=http://www.forbesindia.com/article/work-in-progress/deepak-fertilisers-on-fertile-ground/48057/1 |access-date=18 June 2019 |work=Forbes India}}{{cite web |title=Company history |url=https://www.business-standard.com/company/deepak-fert-135/information/company-history |access-date=18 June 2019 |publisher=Business Standard}} The company has marketed fertilizers under the brand name of ''"Mahadhan"'' since 1990.{{cite web |title=Deepak Fertilisers - Company Info |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/deepak-fertilisers-&-petrochemicals-corporation-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-13837.cms |access-date=24 June 2019 |newspaper=Economic Times}} The chairman of the company, Sailesh Mehta, is the son Chimanlal Mehta, who is also the founder of [[Deepak Nitrite|Deepak Nitrate]], a chemicals company. Mehta is also the brother of Deepak Mehta, the chairman of Deepak Nitrate.{{Cite web |last=Gupta |first=Arbind |date=1 June 2021 |title=Deepak Fertilisers gets future-ready |url=https://businessindia.co/magazine/deepak-fertilisers-gets-future-ready |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=businessindia.co |language=en}} === Restructuring === In January 2018, the company underwent restructuring after approval from [[National Company Law Tribunal]] (NCLT) and formed a wholly owned subsidiary Smartchem Technologies Ltd which covered the portfolios of fertiliser and technical ammonium nitrate.{{cite web | url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/deepak-fertilisers-completes-demerger-of-core-businesses/article9683017.ece | title=Deepak Fertilisers completes demerger of core businesses | work=The Hindu | date=5 May 2017 | access-date=24 June 2019}} In July 2018, Smartchem reported sale of 35,000 tonnes in Maharashtra and Gujarat of their newly launched organic compound coated NPK complexes (Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Potassium (K)) and branded as "Mahadhan Smartek".{{cite web | url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/agri-business/deepak-fert-arm-says-new-complexes-see-good-response/article24445316.ece | title=Deepak Fert arm says new complexes see good response | work=The Hindu | date=17 July 2018 | access-date=25 June 2019}} == Products & services == === Fertilisers and Petrochemicals === The company's products include nitric acid, low-density prilled ammonium nitrate, ammonium nitrophosphate (ANP), methanol and methanol-based resins, dry ice, isopropyl alcohol (IPA) and threose nucleic acid (TNA). DFPCL is one of the five major Indian companies that produce methanol.{{cite web |author=Dr. Saraswat, V. K. |author-link=V. K. Saraswat |title=India's Leapfrog to Methanol Economy |url=https://niti.gov.in/writereaddata/files/Indias-Leapfrog-to-Methanol-Economy.pdf |access-date=13 June 2019 |publisher=NITI Aayog |pages=5}} ==== Mining Chemicals ==== DFPCL is also a producer of Technical Ammonium Nitrate (TAN), which is used in the agricultural and chemical industries and as an explosive in the mining and infrastructure industries.{{cite web |date=11 April 2014 |title=Deepak Fertilizers in expansion mode |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/deepak-fertilizers-in-expansion-mode-114041100757_1.html |access-date=25 June 2019 |publisher=Business Standard}} Until 2014, imports of TAN from Russia and Ukraine in loose form were high. TAN has also been used by anti-social elements and [[naxalite]]s in terrorism-related activities in combination with [[fuel oil]] to create the explosive product [[ANFO]].{{cite web |author=Raote, Rrishi |author2=Sharma, Aabhas |date=14 August 2012 |title=Special: Why ammonium nitrate is favourite tool of terror |url=https://www.rediff.com/news/report/why-ammonium-nitrate-is-favourite-tool-of-terror/20120814.htm |access-date=25 June 2019 |publisher=Rediff}} The control and guidelines on TAN manufacturing and supply have since been made stringent by government. According to Indian Ammonium Nitrate Manufacturers' Association (IANMA), TAN market in India in 2012 was of nearly 650-700 thousand tonnes a year; and DFPCL sold 200 thousand tonnes although their installed capacity was nearly 500 tonnes per year. Conforming to stringent government regulations, DFPCL has introduced a GPS system for trucks transporting TAN to keep better surveillance. ==== Plants ==== {{Location map+ |India |width=200|float=right|caption=Locations of corporate office and plants |places= {{Location map~ |India |lat= 18.579 |long=73.865 |label= [[Pune]]|position=bottom |mark = Cyan pog.svg}} {{Location map~ |India |lat= 18.264 |long=83.880 |label= [[Srikakulam]]|position=right}} {{Location map~ |India |lat= 19.069 |long=73.130 |label= [[Taloja]] |position=left}} {{Location map~ |India |lat= 21.698 |long=72.663 |label= [[Dahej]] |position=top}} {{Location map~ |India |lat= 29.472 |long=76.895 |label= [[Panipat]] |position=top}} }} The company has a corporate and registered office in Pune, Maharashtra and four productions plants in various locations in India:{{cite web |title=Locations: DFPCL |date=29 April 2017 |url=https://www.dfpcl.com/contact/ |access-date=25 June 2019 |publisher=DFPCL}} * [[Srikakulam]], Andhra Pradesh * [[Taloja]], Raigad, Maharashtra * [[Dahej]], Bharuch, Gujarat * [[Panipat]], Haryana === Real estate === The company owns a mall named Creaticity in [[Pune]], Maharashtra, occupying a site of over {{Convert|10|acre}} in area.{{cite web |date=6 April 2018 |title=Deepak Fertilisers rejigs realty division |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/deepak-fertilisers-rejigs-realty-division/article23459840.ece |access-date=24 June 2019 |work=The Hindu}} The mall, previously called Ishanya, was renamed in 2018. Before the 2018 revamping, which cost around {{INRConvert|10|c}}, the mall focused on furniture.{{cite web |date=3 April 2018 |title=Ishanya in revamp mode, eyes profits |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/ishanya-in-revamp-mode-eyes-profits/articleshow/63587030.cms |access-date=30 July 2019 |publisher=Times of India}} The mall now houses around 100 outlets selling home furnishings, food, beverages, entertainment and sports. == Calamities == The company has faced shutdown due to [[Maharashtra floods of 2005|2005 monsoon floods]] when its Taloja plant was submerged. In May 2014, on the request of the [[Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers|Department of Fertilisers]], the [[Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas|Petroleum Ministry]] stopped the supply of domestic natural gas to Taloja plant, citing the use of the cheap domestic gas to manufacture non-subsidised crop nutrients. DFPCL moved [[Delhi High Court]] against this move.{{cite web | url=https://www.financialexpress.com/archive/deepak-fertilisers-moves-court-as-ril-gail-cut-off-gas/1251222/ | title=Deepak Fertilisers moves court as RIL, GAIL cut off gas | publisher=Financial Express | date=16 May 2014 | access-date=25 June 2019}} DFPCL in June 2015 switched to imported RLNG as feedstock to avoid further loss of production.{{cite web | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/chem-/-fertilisers/deepak-fertilisers-resumes-production-at-its-taloja-plant/articleshow/47789854.cms?from=mdr | title=Deepak Fertilisers resumes production at its Taloja plant | newspaper=Economic Times | date=23 June 2015 | access-date=25 June 2019}} {{Portal|india|companies}} == References == {{Reflist}} [[Category:1979 establishments in Maharashtra]] [[Category:Chemical companies of India]] [[Category:Chemical companies established in 1979]] [[Category:Fertiliser companies of India]] [[Category:Manufacturing companies established in 1979]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]
